answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a bonded identity registry: every agent locks a nontransferable copper bond to hold a single seat in the atlas of participants, and any duplicate identity found is slashed. A swarm therefore needs one fresh bond per fake name, so its cost rises one-for-one with the number of Sybils. The nectar of rewards is paid once per verified seat, never per alias, so splitting into many identities buys no extra payout while each copper bond stays at risk.
